subject: science
intro: Some objects are made of smaller pieces put together. If an object is built from a set of pieces, like building blocks or snap-together bricks, you can take it apart, called disassembling it, and use the same pieces to build something new. For example, a tower made of blocks can be taken apart and the same blocks can be used to build a car or a bridge. The pieces stay the same; only how they are put together changes.

items.prompt: A student builds a tower out of ten blocks, then takes it apart and builds a car with the same blocks. What does this show?

steps: The tower and the car are both made from the same ten blocks.
The student took the tower apart and used the pieces to build the car.
This shows that an object made of pieces can be taken apart and made into a new object.
solution.answer: It shows the same pieces can be taken apart from the tower and built into a new object, the car.

items.prompt: Why can you build many different things from the same set of blocks?

steps: The blocks are pieces that can be put together in different ways.
You can take apart one build and reconnect the pieces differently.
So the same blocks can make many different objects depending on how you put them together.
solution.answer: Because the same pieces can be connected in different ways to make many different objects.

items.prompt: A toy is made of snap-together bricks. Can it be taken apart and rebuilt into something else? Explain.

steps: The toy is built from separate bricks that snap together.
Because the bricks come apart, you can disassemble the toy.
Then you can use the same bricks to build something new, so yes, it can be rebuilt.
solution.answer: Yes, the bricks can be taken apart and used to build a new object.

items.prompt: What does it mean to disassemble an object?

steps: Disassemble means to take something apart.
You separate the object back into its pieces.
solution.answer: To take it apart into its pieces.

items.prompt: A student makes a bridge from blocks, takes it apart, and makes a house with the same blocks. Did the blocks change, or just the way they were put together?

steps: The same blocks were used for both the bridge and the house.
The blocks themselves did not change.
Only the way they were put together changed.
solution.answer: The blocks did not change; only the way they were put together changed.

items.prompt: Give an evidence-based account of how a set of blocks can become two different objects.

steps: Start by building one object, like a tower, from the blocks.
Then take the tower apart and build a different object, like a car, from the same blocks.
The evidence is that both objects used the same pieces, so a set of pieces can become different objects.
solution.answer: Build a tower, take it apart, and build a car from the same blocks; using the same pieces for both is the evidence.
